newsitem.title: USA: Dell earnings double in latest quarter, beating estimates.
newsitem.headline: Dell earnings double in latest quarter, beating estimates.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. said Tuesday that second-quarter earnings more than doubled, topping Wall Street estimates and confirming the strong growth trend in the personal computer industry.
Dell said earnings rose to $214 million, or 59 cents a share, from $103 million, or 28 cents a share, a year earlier. According to First Call, the consensus Wall Street estimate was 54 cents a share.
"This is further confirmation that the PC industry is doing fine and we may see some acceleration in the second half of the year," PaineWebber analyst Walter Winnitzki said.
"I think most people were looking for a modest upside and I think most people got what they wanted," he said, referring to analysts and investors on Wall Street.

Dell's earnings were being eyed closely after Hewlett-Packard Co. Monday reported lower-than-expected earnings for the latest quarter. But H-P's results mainly reflected slow sales of medical equipment and higher costs while its personal computer sales remained strong, a trend confirmedt sales growth.
Dell's sales surged to $2.8 billion from $1.7 billion, rising 74 percent to about $2 billion in North and South America and 42 percent to $620 million in Europe.
Revenues jumped 89 percent in the Asia-Pacific region to top $200 million and Dell's Internet web site alone is now generating more than $2 million in sales a day.
Gross margin also rose, climbing to 22.2 percent in the quarter from 21.6 percent in the first quarter of the year.

Over the past year, the top personal computer companies have expanded their dominance of the market, usually at the expense of middle-level PC makers. That shift helped Dell in the first half of its fiscal year, the company said.
"During the first half of fiscal 1998, demand remained solid and the market grew at a healthy pace," Chairman Michael Dell said in a statement.
"The top companies have been consolidating their market share gains during this period and Dell has emerged from this environment as a leader in market share growth," he said.
Analysts said a more profitable product mix helped results, especially new high-end servers used to build corporate computer networks.
Dell stock dipped below $84 in after-hours trading but quickly bounced back near $84.69, where they ended regular trading, up $2.31 on Nasdaq, traders said.
